response:
Reflection on gen-3 results: the archive now has a clear production function. Every top signal is **SUMRANK(R&D-added-back earnings yield, conditioner)**, and the winning conditioners fall into three economically separable families: *funding resilience* (cash × R&D intensity: α 6.9%, t 5.26 — the best in the archive), *book reliability* (peer-excess soft assets α 5.1% t 3.99; goodwill-light + collateral α 6.2% t 5.20), and *moat durability* (margin floor α 5.4% t 4.38; margin CV α 5.2% t 3.86). Two further lessons: additive composites dominate products on alpha, while products dominate on FMB slope (conjunctive peer innovator fmb 6.93), and the time-series cheapness experiment produced alpha (3.4%) but almost no cross-sectional slope, consistent with the critic's reversal interpretation. This batch (i) refines the best conditioner into a single coherent *financial slack* construct rather than stacking cash and leverage separately, (ii) runs one deliberate complementarity test across the two independent reliability families, (iii) asks whether moat durability works through the downside floor or the peer-relative level, and (iv) opens three untested channels: an asset-backing valuation anchor, demand-side customer capital, and R&D–advertising complementarity.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Innovator Financial Slack Value
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: What insures a research program is not gross cash but *net* financial slack — cash minus total debt — because a cash pile offset by maturing obligations cannot fund an unpledgeable investment program; cheap innovators with genuine net slack can sustain research through downturns, while cheap innovators with negative net slack must cut programs or dilute.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive's two strongest conditioners, cash intensity interacted with R&D (α 6.9%) and debt coverage by tangible collateral (α 4.5%), are two halves of one economic quantity, so replacing them with a single net-slack construct is a unification rather than a stack, and it removes the double-counting of firms that hold cash and debt simultaneously. Keeping the multiplicative slack × intensity conditioner preserves the property that financial slack only earns its interpretation for firms actually running a research program.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Reliable Book and Durable Moat Value
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(NEG(IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, 0), at), 1))), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Accounting reliability and economic durability are logically independent failure modes for a value signal — a firm can have a clean, peer-normal balance sheet and still be a commodity price-taker, or hold a genuine moat while its book is inflated by acquisitions — so requiring both should identify cheapness that is simultaneously measured correctly and economically defensible.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a deliberate complementarity test between the two conditioner families that have never been combined, chosen because their inputs share no variables (purchased intangibles versus gross margin history) and their firm rankings should therefore be close to orthogonal, unlike stacking two balance-sheet legs. If the alpha exceeds both parents materially, conditioner information is additive and future work should diversify across families; if it does not, the families are proxies for one latent quality factor, which is equally worth knowing at this stage of the search.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Peer-Excess Pricing Power Value
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Unrecorded intangible capital shows up as the ability to charge more than direct competitors for comparable output, so the informative moat measure is the gross margin in excess of the industry norm, not its time-series behavior; a cheap firm out-earning its peers on margin owns brand or process capital the balance sheet omits.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive has established that margin *dispersion* (CV) and margin *downside* (five-year floor) both work, but both are time-series statistics that require five years of history and cost roughly a point of coverage; this tests whether a purely contemporaneous, peer-relative margin level carries the same information. It also resolves a real ambiguity left by the failed intangible-inclusive gross-profitability signals: those scaled profit by a capital base, whereas margin scales by revenue, and only the latter isolates pricing power rather than capital turnover.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Liquid and Knowledge Asset Backing
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(che, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: For a research-intensive firm the two assets an outside buyer could actually realize are its cash and its accumulated knowledge stock; when the sum of these exceeds a large fraction of market capitalization the market is assigning no value to the operating business, and if that business also sustains a high worst-case gross margin the discount is unwarranted.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This introduces a valuation anchor the archive has never used — realizable liquid plus knowledge assets relative to price, rather than an earnings, sales or book multiple — which is immune to both conservatism (R&D is capitalized in the numerator) and to accrual distortion (cash is objective). The margin floor serves as the economic gate that separates asset-rich firms with a viable business from cash-burning shells whose knowledge stock is being consumed, which was the failure mode of earlier intangible-stock-to-price constructions.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Cheap With Durable Customer Demand
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), NEG(WINSOR(VOL(GROWTH(revt, 1), 5), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Customer capital — installed base, switching costs, recurring relationships — is an unrecorded intangible asset that manifests as revenue that does not lurch with the cycle; a cheap firm with a smooth revenue path owns durable demand, while a cheap firm with volatile revenue is selling into a spot market and its low multiple is compensation for genuine cash-flow risk.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: All validated moat conditioners so far operate on the price side of the income statement (gross margin), leaving the quantity side untested, and the two are economically distinct: a firm can hold margin by shrinking volumes, and stable demand with thin margins is a different asset from cyclical demand with fat margins. Revenue growth volatility is scale-free by construction, so unlike the earlier volatility conditioner it needs no mean normalization and cannot load on firm size.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Dual Intangible Investment Value
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xad, 0), 3), at), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Knowledge capital and brand capital are complements — an invention monetizes only if customers can be reached, and advertising pays only if the product is differentiated — so firms investing materially in both simultaneously build intangible capital that is worth more than the sum of the parts, and their expensed spending depresses reported earnings twice over.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Advertising tested weakly on its own (α 0.9%, t 0.77), but that test used an advertising-based value leg on a 9% coverage subsample, whereas here advertising enters only as a complementarity gate on a full-coverage earnings-yield composite. The multiplicative gate means the long leg contains only genuine dual investors, and a positive result would establish that the intangible-value premium depends on the *composition* of intangible investment rather than its total scale, which no archived signal has tested.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Innovator Financial Slack Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Economically coherent, but this is essentially the archived Cash-Insured Innovation Value (α 6.9%, t 5.26) with `che` swapped for `che − debt` inside the same multiplicative R&D gate and the same value leg — a one-variable substitution that is closer to a cosmetic variant than to the claimed "unification," and the two parents' distinct information (cash buffer vs. debt covered by *tangible* assets, not total assets) is lost rather than combined.

---CRITIQUE Reliable Book and Durable Moat Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: This is a mechanical SUMRANK stack of two already-validated archive legs (Peer-Excess Soft Book Value and Value With a Margin Floor) with no new mechanism, and the nested SUMRANK also halves each conditioner's effective weight relative to its parent, so a null result would be uninformative about the orthogonality claim it is framed to test.

---CRITIQUE Peer-Excess Pricing Power Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Value combined with (industry-adjusted) gross margin level is close to a direct rediscovery of the well-documented gross-profitability/quality-plus-value pairing (Novy-Marx, QMJ), and it is also the most obvious simplification of two already-accepted margin conditioners, so it is both largely known and near-trivial.

---CRITIQUE Liquid and Knowledge Asset Backing---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: The realizable-asset-to-price anchor (cash plus capitalized R&D stock over market cap) is a genuinely different valuation numerator from anything in the archive and the margin-floor gate is a coherent economic screen, though the reviewer should note the numerator's two components each map onto published anomalies (cash-to-price and R&D-to-market), so any result must be checked against those as controls.

---CRITIQUE Cheap With Durable Customer Demand---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Revenue-growth volatility is a quantity-side moat proxy that is economically distinct from the archive's margin-based conditioners, the expression is scale-free and its sign matches the hypothesis, and the only caveat is partial overlap with known fundamental-volatility/quality effects.

---CRITIQUE Dual Intangible Investment Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Because `xad` is missing for the large majority of firms and is coalesced to zero, the advertising leg's RANK degenerates into a reporting-availability/consumer-industry indicator rather than a measure of brand-capital intensity, so the multiplicative "dual investor" gate does not compute what the hypothesis describes.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Innovation Runway Direction
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(TREND(RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), at), 5), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: For a firm whose main asset cannot be pledged, what matters is not the current size of the funding buffer but its direction: an innovator steadily rebuilding net liquidity is generating enough internal cash to keep its program alive indefinitely, while one on a multi-year drawdown is consuming its runway and will be forced into program cuts or dilution before the research pays off.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This is a state-versus-flow change rather than a variable substitution: the archived cash signal measures the level of the buffer at a point in time, whereas the five-year trend in net liquidity measures whether the research program is self-sustaining, and the two can rank the same firm oppositely (cash-rich but depleting versus lean but accumulating). Keeping the multiplicative R&D-intensity gate preserves the interpretation that runway direction is only meaningful for firms actually running an unpledgeable investment program.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Pre-Research Earnings Floor Value
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ebitda, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: The economic engine that produces intangible capital is the firm's pre-research operating profitability, and its worst realized year over a cycle reveals whether that engine can keep funding innovation in a downturn; cheapness backed by a high floor on pre-R&D operating returns is real, while cheapness backed by an engine that has already gone to zero once is compensation for genuine discontinuation risk.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This replaces the mechanical two-winner stack with a single new conditioner that no archived signal contains: a *downside-state* statistic on operating profit measured before intangible investment is expensed, so it neither double-counts the margin floor (which is a revenue-scaled price statistic, not an asset-scaled return) nor reduces to average profitability, since firms with equal mean ROA differ sharply in their worst year. The EBITDA numerator keeps it algebraically distinct from the value leg's income-based numerator, avoiding the shared-input overlap criticized earlier.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Cheap With Uneroded Pricing Power
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUB(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), TS_MAX(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), revt), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Intangible capital depreciates through competitive imitation, and that depreciation is visible as a firm's current gross margin drifting below its own five-year peak; a cheap firm still operating at its historical margin peak retains its moat, whereas a cheap firm far below its own peak is watching its unrecorded capital erode and its low multiple is a forward-looking warning, not a discount.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: Distance-from-own-peak is a depreciation-dynamics measure, not a quality level: it is self-normalizing, so a stable 20%-margin distributor scores as highly as a stable 60%-margin software firm, which is exactly what separates it from the gross-profitability/QMJ pairing the critic identified. It is also economically distinct from the accepted margin floor, which rewards a high worst-case level, whereas this rewards the *absence of decay* regardless of level, so together the two will tell us whether moat strength or moat trajectory carries the information.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Peer-Excess Brand Investment Value
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), IND_ADJ(WINSOR(RATIO(MA(xad, 3), sale), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Among firms for which advertising is a genuine strategic input, spending more on brand building than industry peers creates customer capital that is expensed immediately and absent from book value, so the cheap heavy advertiser within a consumer-facing industry is systematically undervalued relative to its peers.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The critic is right that coalescing missing advertising to zero turns the leg into a reporting-availability dummy, so this version does not coalesce: the signal is defined only where advertising is actually reported, and IND_ADJ then measures brand investment relative to the industry norm rather than relative to firms for which advertising is not a decision variable. Coverage will fall to roughly the advertiser subsample, which is the economically correct universe for this hypothesis and is the same universe in which any brand-capital effect could plausibly exist.
